decisions.evidence: EW ExampleC.14(3)–(4) (PDF169/printed438) needs a nontrivial character of a general local field and computes Qp. None of the four retained B examples has a local-field variable or p-adic topology. The Euclidean finite-product argument uses only additive real lines.

decisions.name: §4.23, Theorem 4.26: translation between regular blocks with W_λ = W_μ is an equivalence
decisions.reason: The pair does not claim the block equivalence; it only uses the standard-module and simplicity behaviour across a single wall, which is proved from the Verma-flag computation.
decisions.evidence: Gaitsgory4.26 (PDF24–25) gives quasi-inverse translation equivalences between certain regular blocks. The selected proof of enough projectives uses a self-dual finite tensor of a maximal-label Verma and the exact block projection, not a translation equivalence. The wall theorem only promises image standards and two-factor flags.

decisions.name: C.3, Theorem C.6: a subgroup of the dual separating points is dense
decisions.reason: Density of separating subgroups is used together with inversion and biduality on the planned duality pair and is not needed for the closure, local-compactness or example claims of FR-15.
decisions.evidence: EW C.6 (PDF165/printed434) contains both dual local compactness and density of a separating subgroup. Current thm-dual-of-an-lca-group-is-locally-compact-abelian proves the former from Ascoli. No proper subgroup of the dual is asserted dense, so the latter may be reserved for inversion/biduality.

decisions.name: §1, the implication (c)⇒(a) in Theorem-Definition 1.1 (devissage producing a standard filtration)
decisions.reason: The pair never needs to construct a standard filtration from Ext vanishing; it only needs the multiplicity formula and Ext^1 vanishing for objects already known to be standardly filtered, so this converse is not consumed.
decisions.evidence: Lin9 Theorem-Definition1.1(c)⇒(a) (PDF3) constructs a standard flag for an arbitrary Ext1-acyclic object. The selected claims require flags for projectives only, provided by the finite tensor-Verma/direct-summand construction. After correcting maximal versus greatest in the peeling supplier, that direct construction handles incomparable maximal labels and does not need this converse criterion.

decisions.name: Bochner's theorem on finite groups and the transition to LCA Fourier–Stieltjes transforms, pp. 8–14
decisions.reason: The fetched edition of the notes cited as 'Taob note 9' contains no restriction or Strichartz material; the Strichartz interface is sourced instead to Williams §11.4. No FR-14 item depends on this source.
decisions.evidence: Tao9 PDF8–14 develops positive-definite functions, Bochner, preliminary LCA inversion and Walsh examples. The only forward dispersive orientation in FR14 is explicitly recorded as proved_here:false; endpoint restriction itself is established by the Williams slice/HLS proof. Bochner is neither a Fourier-restriction assertion nor an operative prerequisite here.

decisions.name: Section 7.1, Corollary 7.3: the inclusion of the dual into the compact group of all homomorphisms is an embedding iff the group is discrete
decisions.reason: This criterion compares the dual with all possibly discontinuous homomorphisms; no scaffolded FR-15 item or later consumer uses it, and it contributes nothing to local compactness or to the four examples.
decisions.evidence: Dikranjan Corollary7.3 (PDF52/printed48) adds the converse that the inclusion into all homomorphisms is an embedding only for discrete G. The selected discrete-domain lemma proves the forward equality of compact-open and product topologies by finite compact sets; the compact/discrete theorem proves only the two direct implications. Neither asserts this general converse.

decisions.name: §1, Lemma 1.5: generalized Verma modules M_{λ,n} admit standard filtrations
decisions.reason: This serves Lin Chen's alternative proof that projectives are standardly filtered; the pair proves that theorem through finite-dimensional tensoring of maximal-label Vermas, so this engine has no consumer.
decisions.evidence: Lin9 Lemma1.5 (PDF1–2) constructs generalized-Verma standard flags, an alternative route. The owner-approved replacement tensor-reach item now proves the full arbitrary-weight construction: a finite-W root-coordinate bound makes λ maximal in its actual integral-reflection block, the maximal-Verma weight-functor proof and exact block projection make it ambient-projective, and E*=E gives the nonzero highest-vector tensor mapping onto Lμ. thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags then uses the fully proved tensor-Verma filtration and the corrected maximal-label direct-summand lemma. Every commissioned projective/flag conclusion is retained, so generalized-Vermas supply no missing prerequisite.

decisions.name: §4.23, Lemma 4.25: a vanishing criterion for T_{χ1,V,χ2}
decisions.reason: The pair only needs the standard-module behaviour on a single wall and the adjunction; the general vanishing criterion for arbitrary translation functors is not used.
decisions.evidence: Gaitsgory Lemma4.25 (PDF24) is a general vanishing criterion for an arbitrary translation functor if no compatible tensor weight exists. The single-wall selected theorem computes exactly the compatible weights using local norm/exclusion lemmas and retains target central-character factors. It does not state the general zero-functor criterion.

decisions.name: Exercise 3.20 (printed pp. 9–10), Theorem 4.37 and Corollary 4.40 (printed pp. 29–31): closed subgroups of R and Rn and the structure of Rn/H
decisions.reason: The actual Dikranjan closed-subgroup and quotient classification is not needed by the selected real-character covering/Cauchy proof or the finite-coordinate Euclidean-dual computation.
decisions.evidence: The corrected Dikranjan Exercise3.20 (PDF13–14) and Theorem4.37/Corollary4.40 (PDF33–35) were inspected. They classify closed real/Euclidean subgroups and quotient groups. The current real-character lemma instead lifts through R→R/Z and applies the continuous Cauchy equation, and the Euclidean-dual example uses a finite coordinate product; neither imports subgroup classification. This exact source-locator repair removes the unsupported old numbering without dropping a commissioned prerequisite.

decisions.name: §16.3, Corollary 16.6(ii): every projective object is a free U(n−)-module
decisions.reason: Not needed by any claim of this pair. The free-U(n−) structure serves Etingof's Lemma 20.1 route to Ext vanishing, while the pair proves the Δ–∇ orthogonality by Lin Chen's pullback argument and never uses freeness over U(n−).
decisions.evidence: Etingof Corollary16.6(ii) (PDF88/printed87) says every projective is U(n−)-free. The commissioned projective theorem requires finite Verma flags, and its local proof uses a tensor-Verma filtration and closure under direct summands. It never invokes freeness of arbitrary projectives or graded projective-module classification.

decisions.name: §24.2, two-sided ideals in U_θ and submodules of Verma modules
decisions.reason: This section studies the classification of projective functors and the KL problem; nothing in the pair's inventory or examples consumes its results.

decisions.name: Sections 7.4-8, natural transformation, duality theorem 7.36, structure and exactness
decisions.reason: Biduality, exactness and the natural transformation are exactly the subject of that planned pair; the present foundation stops before inversion and biduality by design.

Current pullback identity/composition and the quotient-annihilator embedding are proved locally without that duality. Those limited assertions remain included; double-dual surjectivity and full structure are outside FR15.

decisions.name: C.3, Theorem C.10 (printed p. 436): Fourier inversion on L1(G) intersect B(G)
decisions.reason: The actual EW inversion theorem concerns a Haar Fourier transform and the positive-definite class B(G); FR15 constructs the dual topologically without an inversion assertion. FR16 is the approved inversion destination.
decisions.evidence: The complete EW Theorem C.10 at PDF167/printed436 was inspected: it normalizes dual Haar measure and gives Fourier inversion for L1(G) intersect B(G). The selected topological character foundation neither defines that transform theorem nor invokes inversion; FR16 explicitly owns it. This verified actual-source row replaces the unavailable Koerner chapter claim and the previous incorrectly combined C.10/C.12 destination.

decisions.name: Section 7.3, Theorem 7.14 second part: the dual of a product of compact groups is the direct sum of the duals
decisions.reason: Compact-product duality is not needed for the four concrete examples and is subsumed by the later biduality and exactness development of the planned duality pair.
decisions.evidence: Dikranjan7.14 second part (PDF55/printed51) computes the dual of an arbitrary compact product as an algebraic direct sum, using finite coordinate support of a continuous character. The selected lemma claims finite products plus the dual of a discrete direct sum; it never claims this arbitrary compact-product converse. Its finite restriction/product proof and discrete-source continuity are complete.
